scope: Native GuitarHub popular-song practice companions: six modules, twenty-four recognizable songs, and six original preparation checkpoints. External external guitar tutorials remain the source for actual song arrangements.

instructionConventions.boundary: Every song entry is an original preparation exercise. The linked external creator page is the actual song lesson.
instructionConventions.practiceSpec: Rhythm targets are counted attacks in the authored original drill only; they do not measure chords, tone, lyrics, riffs, arrangement, or full-song mastery.
instructionConventions.timing: Every rhythm spec uses a four-beat count-in, 32 targets, cue text, pass score 80, and completionMinimumBPM equal to the authored BPM.
instructionConventions.rights: No lyrics, distinctive riffs, full transcriptions, copied media, or proprietary behavior are included.

integrationNote.loader: Merge this TrackPath and LessonInstructionLibrary by ID with the base guitar catalog during integration.
integrationNote.access: Level g-songs is intended for the paid guided catalog; host entitlement controls access.
integrationNote.assets: Each song has two chord_diagram_and_reference_tones assets and one external_practice_links asset.

steps.title: Set the reference frame
steps.action: Tune to standard tuning, set a four-beat count-in, and write Em7, G, D, A7sus4 on a card. Keep this session focused on the authored preparation drill.
steps.lookCheck: The guitar and chord card are stable, your picking arm is loose, and your fretting thumb rests lightly behind the neck.
steps.listenCheck: You can count 1–2–3–4 evenly before making the first attack.

steps.title: Place every chord in the drill
steps.action: Read strings 6 (thickest) through 1 (thinnest). Fingers 1–4 are index, middle, ring and little. Em7 — 6: open; 5: fret 2, finger 2; 4: open; 3: open; 2: open; 1: open. G — 6: fret 3, finger 2; 5: fret 2, finger 1; 4: open; 3: open; 2: open; 1: fret 3, finger 3. D — 6: mute; 5: mute; 4: open; 3: fret 2, finger 1; 2: fret 3, finger 3; 1: fret 2, finger 2. A7sus4 — 6: mute; 5: open; 4: fret 2, finger 2; 3: open; 2: fret 3, finger 3; 1: fret 3, finger 4. Pick each sounding string slowly, then release and rebuild.
steps.lookCheck: Each fingertip lands close behind its fret and muted strings remain silent.
steps.listenCheck: Each shape has a separate usable sound; a buzz is a cue to move nearer the fret and reduce pressure.

steps.title: Run the authored four-bar study
steps.action: At 72 BPM, play one four-beat bar each of Em7, G, D, A7sus4, then repeat once: eight bars and 32 attacks after a four-beat count-in. Strum down on 1, 2, 3 and 4. Float upward silently between strokes. This original preparation drill is separate from the external song arrangement.
steps.lookCheck: Your fretting hand prepares the next shape during the final beat without the picking hand rushing.
steps.listenCheck: The one quarter-note downstroke per beat while the forearm travels in eighths stays audible and the four-count remains steady. The microphone result covers attack timing only.

steps.title: Compare with the external lesson
steps.action: Open the linked Oasis external guitar tutorial after stopping the in-app drill. Note its tuning, capo, arrangement, and difficulty; choose one small idea to explore later.
steps.lookCheck: You can name which part is your own study and which information comes from the external page.
steps.listenCheck: You can hear one difference between your preparation rhythm and the source arrangement without claiming a full-song performance.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The change arrives late or the hand stops.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Mute the strings, speak four counts, and practice only the two-shape change at half the authored BPM for three loops before restoring the study.

mistakeRecovery.observation: A chord buzzes or an unintended string rings.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Return to Em and G one string at a time. Move fingertips nearer the fret wire, arch neighboring fingers, and test before adding the next string.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The external lesson feels crowded.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Close the external page, return to the 32-count original study, and remove embellishments. Reopen the source only when the plain counted pulse feels comfortable.
